 Save your program as Question3_J26.

stem_ctx:
A prototype for a game is designed using Object‑Oriented Programming (OOP).
    The game will allow a character to move along a path (for example a road or sidewalk).
    The prototype requires the classes setting up and the path creating ready for the character to
    be implemented.

Each space in the path can contain an object. The path and objects are created as classes.
        The class TheObject stores the data about the objects. The attributes are public.
                                        TheObject
 ObjectType : String             stores the type of object, either "Money" or "Experience"
 Amount : Integer                stores the amount of the object, for example 200
 Constructor()                    initialises the attributes to the parameter values
    The class Path stores the data about the objects. The attributes are public.
                                           Path
 BoardArray[0:99] : TheObject  an array of 100 objects of type TheObject
 NumberSpaces : Integer         stores the number of spaces in the path
 Constructor()                    initialises NumberSpaces to the parameter value.
                                     Initialises all 100 array objects to an empty object of type
                                     TheObject. An empty object has the values
                                     ObjectType = "" and Amount = –1
 GetNumberSpaces()               returns NumberSpaces
 InitialiseData()                takes an array of objects of type TheObject as a
                                     parameter and stores them in BoardArray
 ReturnPath()                     returns a string created using data from each object
                                     in BoardArray
 GetPathObject()                 takes a number as a parameter and returns the object in
                                     that index in BoardArray

Constructor header (and end)
… taking 2 parameters …
… assigning parameters to attributes
